SYNTHESIZED — no real Codex CLI transcript was available on this machine.

This fixture mimics the native shape of the Codex CLI session store
`~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl` (one JSON object per line),
following the Task B3 brief: `response` / `function_call` /
`function_call_output` / `compacted` record types carrying `cwd`,
`session_id`, `version`, and `timestamp` on every record, plus the two
companion shapes the mapping requires — `prompt` records (user input text)
and `reasoning` records (reasoning summaries).

- `prompt.text` mimics the user-prompt payload.
- `response` mimics a model turn: `text`, `model`, and token `usage`
  (`input_tokens` / `output_tokens` / `cache_*`). The optional
  `reasoning_summary` field is a tolerance affordance so one record can
  carry two events (message + reasoning); it exercises the multi-event
  resume path in the incremental test.
- `function_call` mimics the OpenAI function-call shape: `name` plus
  `arguments` as a JSON-encoded string (an object is also accepted).
- `function_call_output.output` mimics the tool result payload.
- `compacted.summary` mimics the rolling-window compaction record. It sits
  mid-file (record 7 of 8, with a `prompt` after it) to pin that the
  adapter emits every record exactly once in file order — never reordered,
  never dropped.

Model name (`gpt-5-codex`), versions, token counts, and prose are invented.
